title: Power Mean Limits: Formal Proof via Filter.Tendsto
description: Fully formalizes the extreme cases of the power mean: lim_{r→+∞} M_r = max(x₁,...,xₙ) and lim_{r→-∞} M_r = min(x₁,...,xₙ). Uses Mathlib's Filter.Tendsto and Real.rpow to give a complete squeeze-theorem proof.

meta.author: Hardy-Littlewood-Pólya (1934); Lean formalization 2026
meta.assumptions: None. 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Complete formalization using Mathlib's Filter.Tendsto, Real.rpow, and Finset.sup'/inf'.
originalContributions: Self-contained reproof of the extreme power-mean limits (M_r → max as r → +∞, M_r → min as r → -∞) using only Mathlib's Filter.Tendsto and Real.rpow, with no dependency on the parallel formalization in AmgmInequalityOQ03OQ02OQ04.lean (which uses Filter.tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop). This entry provides the alternative formulation via the duality identity M_{-r}(x) = M_r(1/x)⁻¹.

The auxiliary helper `tendsto_rpow_inv_atTop` (c^{1/r} → 1 as r → +∞) is proved directly via c^{1/r} = exp(log(c) · r⁻¹) and continuity of exp at 0 — an elementary route that avoids the c^(−r⁻¹) reformulation used in the OQ-04 sibling.
Explicit min-max duality identity minX(x) = (maxX(1/x))⁻¹ proved through Finset.sup'/inf' rather than reduction to a single existing Mathlib lemma.
prerequisites: Power mean definition M_r(x) = ((Σ xᵢ^r) / n)^{1/r} on a finite, nonempty index type ι (defined in this file)
Finset.sup'/inf' for max/min over a nonempty finite type

mathlibDependencies.description: Monotonicity of x ↦ x^r for r ≥ 0 and 0 ≤ x. Underlies both M_le_maxX (upper bound) and maxX_mul_rpow_le_M (lower bound).
(x⁻¹)^r = (x^r)⁻¹ and x^(-r) = (x^r)⁻¹ for 0 ≤ x. The algebraic core of the duality identity M_{-r}(x) = M_r(1/x)⁻¹.
Continuity of r ↦ c^r and r ↦ exp(r), used to lift r⁻¹ → 0 through the exponent in tendsto_rpow_inv_atTop.
Filter version of the squeeze theorem with eventual (not pointwise) bounds. Enables the squeeze in tendsto_M_atTop between maxX · n^{-1/r} and the constant maxX.
Negation maps Filter.atBot to Filter.atTop. Used in tendsto_M_atBot to reduce r → -∞ to the previously-proved r → +∞ case.
Maximum and minimum over a nonempty Finset. Underlie maxX and minX definitions and the algebraic identity minX(x) = (maxX(1/x))⁻¹.

overview.historicalContext: The power mean (generalized mean) M_r(x₁,...,xₙ) = ((Σxᵢʳ)/n)^{1/r} interpolates continuously between the minimum (r → -∞), geometric mean (r → 0), arithmetic mean (r = 1), quadratic mean (r = 2), and maximum (r → +∞). Hardy, Littlewood, and Pólya established the monotonicity and limit behavior in their 1934 treatise 'Inequalities'. The formal verification of the limit cases requires combining squeeze theorem arguments with continuity of Real.rpow and the algebraic duality M_{-r}(x) = 1/M_r(1/x).
overview.problemStatement:
For positive reals x₁,...,xₙ and the power mean M_r = ((Σxᵢʳ)/n)^{1/r}, prove:
(1) lim_{r→+∞} M_r = max(x₁,...,xₙ)
(2) lim_{r→-∞} M_r = min(x₁,...,xₙ)
Using Lean 4 / Mathlib's Filter.Tendsto, Real.rpow, and Finset.sup'/inf'.
overview.proofStrategy: For (1): Squeeze M_r between max · n^{-1/r} (lower bound, via the maximum term dominating the sum) and max (upper bound, since each xᵢʳ ≤ maxʳ). Both bounds converge to max since n^{-1/r} → 1. This uses tendsto_rpow_inv_atTop (proved from c^{1/r} = exp(log(c)/r) → exp(0) = 1). For (2): Use the duality M_{-r}(x) = (M_r(1/x))⁻¹ and the min = (max(1/x))⁻¹ identity, then deduce the -∞ limit from the +∞ result via negation (tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop).
keyInsights: The key helper tendsto_rpow_inv_atTop ({c > 0} : c^{r⁻¹} → 1 as r → +∞) is proved by writing c^{r⁻¹} = exp(log(c) · r⁻¹) and using continuity of exp at 0.
The squeeze theorem (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le') gives the +∞ limit cleanly: lower bound maxX · n^{-1/r} → maxX and upper bound M_r ≤ maxX (constant), both verified.
The duality M_{-r}(x) = (M_r(1/x))⁻¹ (proved via inv_rpow and rpow_neg) reduces the -∞ case to the +∞ case with 1/x substituted.
The identity minX(x) = (maxX(1/x))⁻¹ (proved via Finset.sup'/inf' manipulations and aux_inv_le_inv) completes the min limit.

The formal limit M_r → max as r → +∞ captures the intuition that large positive exponents emphasize the largest component — the L^∞ norm of the vector of weights — connecting power means to the theory of L^p spaces as p → ∞
prerequisites: Real.rpow and its properties (rpow_le_rpow, rpow_mul, rpow_neg, inv_rpow)
Finset.sup'/inf' for max/min over finite types

sections.title: Helper Lemmas
sections.summary: tendsto_rpow_inv_atTop (c^{1/r} → 1 as r → +∞) and rpow_le_rpow_of_nonpos (monotone rpow for nonpositive exponents).
sections.mathContext: $c^{r^{-1}} = e^{(\log c)/r} \to e^0 = 1$ as $r \to +\infty$ (continuity of $\exp$ at 0). For $0 < a \leq b$ and $z \leq 0$: $b^z \leq a^z$ (proved via $z = -(-z)$ and `rpow_neg`).

sections.title: Max Bound Theorems
sections.summary: M_le_maxX (M_r ≤ max for r > 0) and maxX_mul_rpow_le_M (max · n^{-1/r} ≤ M_r for r > 0).
sections.mathContext: Upper: $x_i^r \leq (\max x)^r$ for all $i$, so $M_r \leq (\max x)^{r \cdot 1/r} = \max x$. Lower: the maximizer $x_{i_0}$ satisfies $(\max x)^r / n \leq \frac{\sum x_i^r}{n}$, giving $\max x \cdot n^{-1/r} \leq M_r$.

sections.title: Limit as r → +∞
sections.summary: tendsto_M_atTop: M_r → max as r → +∞. Proved by squeeze theorem using the two bounds.
sections.mathContext: Squeeze: $\max x \cdot n^{-1/r} \leq M_r \leq \max x$ and $n^{-1/r} \to 1$, so both bounds tend to $\max x$. Uses `tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le'` with eventual (not pointwise) bounds.

sections.title: Duality and Min
sections.mathContext: $M_{-r}(x) = \left(\frac{\sum x_i^{-r}}{n}\right)^{-1/r} = \left[\left(\frac{\sum (x_i^{-1})^r}{n}\right)^{1/r}\right]^{-1} = M_r(1/x)^{-1}$. Also: $\min_i x_i = (\max_i x_i^{-1})^{-1}$ for positive $x_i$.

sections.title: Limit as r → -∞
sections.summary: tendsto_M_atBot: M_r → min as r → -∞. Proved via duality from the +∞ result.
sections.mathContext: $M_r(x) \to \min x$ as $r \to -\infty$. Proof: set $y_i = 1/x_i$; from $M_s(y) \to \max(y)$ as $s \to +\infty$, invert and compose with $r \mapsto -r$ via `tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop`.

conclusion.summary: Complete formalization (0 sorries, 0 axioms) of the power mean limit theorems lim_{r→±∞} M_r = max/min using Mathlib's Filter.Tendsto framework and Real.rpow. The proof uses a squeeze-theorem approach for +∞ and algebraic duality for -∞.
conclusion.implications: Together with the monotonicity M_r ≤ M_s (r ≤ s), this completes the picture of the power mean as a continuous interpolation from min to max. These limits appear in worst-case analysis, the theory of Lp spaces (as p → ∞, the Lp norm approaches the L∞/sup norm), and in information theory (Rényi entropy limits).
openQuestions: Can the geometric mean case (r → 0) be handled by continuity of r ↦ M_r, avoiding the conditional branch in the definition?
Is there a unified proof covering all of AM-GM-Power mean monotonicity (M_r ≤ M_s for r ≤ s) using Mathlib's Jensen inequality or convexity infrastructure?

mainTheorems.name: tendsto_rpow_inv_atTop
mainTheorems.description: Key auxiliary: for any c > 0, c^{1/r} → 1 as r → +∞. Proved via c^{1/r} = exp(log(c) · r⁻¹) and continuity of exp at 0.
mainTheorems.leanType: {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) → Filter.Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => c ^ r⁻¹) Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

mainTheorems.name: M_le_maxX
mainTheorems.description: Upper bound for the squeeze: for r > 0, M_r(x) ≤ max(x). Each xᵢ^r ≤ (max x)^r combined with normalization yields M_r ≤ max.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hr : 0 < r) → M x r ≤ maxX x

mainTheorems.name: maxX_mul_rpow_le_M
mainTheorems.description: Lower bound for the squeeze: for r > 0, max(x) · n^{-1/r} ≤ M_r(x). Single-term contribution from the maximizer plus normalization gives the lower envelope.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) (hr : 0 < r) → maxX x * (Fintype.card ι : ℝ) ^ (-r⁻¹) ≤ M x r

mainTheorems.name: tendsto_M_atTop
mainTheorems.description: Main +∞ limit: M_r(x) → max(x) as r → +∞. Squeezed between maxX · n^{-1/r} → maxX (using tendsto_rpow_inv_atTop) and the constant maxX.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) → Filter.Tendsto (M x) Filter.atTop (nhds (maxX x))

mainTheorems.name: M_neg_eq_inv_M_inv
mainTheorems.description: Duality identity: M_{-r}(x) = M_r(1/x)⁻¹ for r ≠ 0 and positive x. Reduces the -∞ case to the +∞ case under the substitution x ↦ 1/x.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) {r : ℝ} (hr : r ≠ 0) → M x (-r) = (M (fun i => (x i)⁻¹) r)⁻¹

mainTheorems.name: minX_eq_inv_maxX_inv
mainTheorems.description: Min–max duality on positive reals: min(x) = (max(1/x))⁻¹. Proved via Finset.sup'/inf' manipulations and antitone inversion.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) → minX x = (maxX (fun i => (x i)⁻¹))⁻¹

mainTheorems.name: tendsto_M_atBot
mainTheorems.description: Main -∞ limit: M_r(x) → min(x) as r → -∞. Combines M_neg_eq_inv_M_inv, minX_eq_inv_maxX_inv, the +∞ result for 1/x, and Filter.tendsto_neg_atBot_atTop.
mainTheorems.leanType: (hx : ∀ i, 0 < x i) → Filter.Tendsto (M x) Filter.atBot (nhds (minX x))
